origin.name: OCLP's OpenCore config.plist for the target's model, as pipeline/stages/build-efi.py generates it
origin.note: in the image's EFI partition, not in the System volume. Not declared here (no edit kind for it yet): the HaoExec.kext entry appended to Kernel.Add (plist.set cannot append), the Kernel.Patch that keeps AMFI's dyld environment policy for hardened programs (src/amfi_dyld.py binds it to the linked BootKC, as kc.bind does the repairs), and RSRHelper, KDKlessWorkaround and CatalinaIntelI210Ethernet set Enabled false in Kernel.Add (an edit by bundle name, which plist.set's index keys cannot say). The boot-args value is the end-user one; dev-diagnostics (pack dev) adds the measurement switches in dev images

edits.reason: the Darwin 27 kernel starts on Ivy Bridge: the kernel repairs in Kernel.Patch (on 26B131: early VM range initialization, ascending early kernel-map bounds, the bootstrap physical-page alias code and its registration call) and the IntelCommpage.kext Kernel.Add entry, computed by tools/kc-binder from the BootKC this image links
edits.evidence: apply.sh runs src/kc_bind.py on the image's BootKernelExtensions.kc, which refuses unless kc-binder's config.plist is byte-identical to the recorded kernel_repair_efi repairs src/repair_binding.py binds to that BootKC (or, when those refuse it, unless IntelCommpage's compiled addresses hold for it); src/repairs.py installs the result. tests/test_kc_bind.py (HAO_OPENCORE_BOOT_KC and the row variables) proves the bytes on the recorded 26B131 collections

edits.reason: an end-user image writes no OpenCore log and shows no OpenCore text (Target 0: logging off; it also saves the file writes at every boot); dev sets get the file log from dev-diagnostics (pack dev)

the Intel Mac boots Darwin 27 with its Lilu-based drivers loading, hao's arm64-only programs allowed to start, entitled programs keeping DYLD_* variables out, a panic rebooting instead of waiting for a debugger, and kernelmanagerd loading the System kernel collection without first trying, and failing, to build an auxiliary collection

arg_reasons.keepsyms=1: OCLP's base config: a panic report keeps the kernel's symbols, so it names functions instead of bare addresses
arg_reasons.-lilubetaall: Lilu and its plug-ins (OCLP's graphics and hardware kexts) load although they do not list Darwin 27 as supported
arg_reasons.ipc_control_port_options=0: OCLP adds it whenever SIP is lowered (efi_builder/security.py): from macOS 12.3 Electron apps stop launching with SIP lowered unless the IPC control-port policy is relaxed
arg_reasons.amfi_get_out_of_my_way=1: macos27tool-runtime signs each program's x86_64 slice ad hoc with that program's own entitlements, including Apple-private ones (launchd's); with AMFIPass alone AMFI rejects /sbin/launchd and the kernel panics
arg_reasons.amfi_force_policy=8: AMFI's dyld policy treats a restricted program (CS_RESTRICT: it holds entitlements) as restricted again although SIP's filesystem bit is allowed, as on a Mac with SIP on, so dyld denies it the DYLD_* path variables (DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES, library and framework paths) unless it also requires library validation, which keeps them as on a Mac with SIP on (owner D1, 2026-11-17). Not version-scoped: a Recovery booted through this OpenCore gets it too; the Recovery tools that insert libraries run in the NetBoot Recovery, whose config is OCLP's. Bit 0x8 of AMFI's force_policy (forceDefaultDyldEnvVarsPolicy) is read only by the dyld environment policy; nothing the image ships sets DYLD_* for an entitled program
arg_reasons.auxKCAtBoot=false: kernelmanagerd loads the System kernel collection at once instead of first building an auxiliary one: 27's kmutil cannot build an x86_64 collection, so that build failed at every boot and held the System collection (and with it the framebuffer and WindowServer) back about 18 s

edits.reason: OpenCore deletes the stored boot-args and csr-active-config before writing its own, so the image's values apply (bootercfg and bootercfg-once, a boot-logging investigation's, are no longer deleted: leftover-settings audit, 2026-11-17)
a normal boot shows only the Apple logo (owner 2026-11-13): no boot.efi or apfs.efi debug lines; the OpenCore archive is the RELEASE build unless the assembly asks for debug
